CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_CGROUP_EXCLUDE
to a comma-separated list of the kinds to exempt from the cap; Claude Code applies the cap to every kind not on your list. Set it to
none
to cap every kind, or to
all-new
to cap only Bash, PowerShell, and Monitor tool commands. Requires Claude Code v2.1.246 or later. The kinds you can name:
mcp
: local
MCP servers
lsp
:
language servers
hooks
:
hook
commands
plugin
: commands that
plugins
run
helper
: Claude Code’s own helper commands, such as
git
agent
: child Claude Code processes, such as
agent teammates
Whatever you list, these rules apply:
Unknown names
: Claude Code ignores names it doesn’t recognize
Variable unset
: Claude Code takes the set of other capped kinds from configuration Anthropic delivers from the server, and that set can change over time, so set the variable when you need a set that doesn’t change
Permission-gating hooks
: even with every kind capped, Claude Code excludes from the cap a hook that can block or change the outcome of an action, and any MCP server that such a hook calls, so the kernel killing a permission-gating hook can’t allow the action it was blocking
#### Edit tool behavior
The Edit tool performs exact string replacement. It takes an
old_string
and a
new_string
and replaces the first with the second. It doesn’t use regex or fuzzy matching.
These checks must pass for an edit to apply. Before any of them, a path matched by a
Read
deny rule
is refused, including creating a new file there.
Read-before-edit
: Claude reads the file in the current conversation before editing it, and a read cut short with a
PARTIAL view
notice
doesn’t count. Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Haiku 4.5, and older models always require the read. Newer models can edit an unread file when reading it wouldn’t need a permission prompt and the Read tool is available.
Match
:
old_string
must appear in the file exactly as written. A single character of whitespace or indentation difference is enough to miss.
Uniqueness
:
old_string
must appear exactly once. When it appears more than once, Claude either supplies a longer string with enough surrounding context to pin down one occurrence, or sets
replace_all: true
to replace them all.
A file that changed on disk after Claude last read it can still be edited when
old_string
matches the current content exactly and unambiguously and Claude Code can read the file without prompting. Matching against the file’s current content keeps this safe, and the result notes that the file carries other changes so Claude re-reads it before edits that depend on surrounding content. In any other case, such as a stale
old_string
or one that matches more than once without
replace_all
, Claude reads the file again before editing.
Claude can also edit a file without a separate Read after viewing it with a Bash command such as
cat
or
grep
. Those commands are
cat
,
nl
,
bat
,
batcat
,
head
,
tail
,
sed -n 'X,Yp'
,
grep
,
egrep
,
fgrep
, and
rg
, each run on one file with no pipes or redirects. If the command printed none of the file’s text, as when a search matches nothing, the read-before-edit check still applies.
When Claude views a file this way, Claude Code also loads any
subdirectory
CLAUDE.md
and
path-scoped rules
that apply to that file. See
Read and Edit permission rules
for which Bash commands your
Read
and
Edit
deny rules cover.
##### Protect read-only files in Perforce
To keep Edit, Write, and NotebookEdit from overwriting read-only files in a Perforce workspace, set
CLAUDE_CODE_PERFORCE_MODE
to
1
. Those tools then refuse to change read-only files and tell Claude to run
p4 edit
first.
##### Non-UTF-8 files
Claude can’t use
NotebookEdit
on a file that isn’t valid UTF-8. The same goes for Edit, unless the file starts with a little-endian UTF-16 byte-order mark. When Claude tries, the tool refuses the change and leaves the file untouched. Refused files include non-ASCII text saved in a legacy encoding such as Windows-1252 or Shift-JIS, binary files, and UTF-8 with an invalid byte sequence.
The tools refuse because they save the whole file back as UTF-8, which would replace every byte they can’t decode with the replacement character
U+FFFD
. Instead, the
error Claude receives
tells it to make the change with a shell command that keeps the file’s encoding, or to ask you about converting it to UTF-8 first.
Claude can still replace such a file with Write, unless the new content contains
U+FFFD
, the character Read shows Claude in place of bytes it can’t decode. That guard stops Claude from writing back the garbled text it read. When Write does replace the file, it saves the new content as UTF-8, so the file’s original encoding is lost.
#### EndConversation tool behavior
The EndConversation tool ends the current session. Claude uses it only in two situations:
When you keep sending abusive messages after Claude gives a clear warning and fails to redirect the conversation
When you explicitly ask Claude to end the session, then confirm when Claude asks whether you still want to proceed
General frustration, profanity, or a task going badly don’t qualify, and neither do requests for harmful content, which Claude declines instead of ending the session. Claude Code follows the same approach as claude.ai, which can
end a rare subset of chats
.
After Claude ends an interactive session, the session locks. New prompts and most commands return
Claude ended this conversation. Start a new session (or /clear) to continue.
, and only
/clear
,
/resume
,
/help
,
/exit
, and
/feedback
still run. Claude Code records the end in the session’s transcript, so resuming an ended session restores the lock; the session’s history isn’t deleted.
Resuming an ended session in
non-interactive mode
with the
-p
flag errors and exits with code 1, so a script doesn’t read the ended run as a success.
The tool never prompts for permission, and
PreToolUse hooks
don’t run for it. While any other tool remains, you can’t block it either:
deny and ask rules
naming
EndConversation
have no effect, and neither
--disallowedTools
nor a
--tools
list can remove it. The exemption is deliberate: the tool does nothing except end the conversation, never reading or modifying files or data, and a safeguard of this kind holds only if the session it applies to can’t turn it off. When your deny rules remove every other tool and also match
EndConversation
, as
"*"
does, Claude Code removes it too rather than leaving it as the only tool, unless an allow rule names
EndConversation
explicitly. A deny list that removes every other tool without matching
EndConversation
leaves it in place.
Subagents
never get the tool. Background tasks that share the main conversation’s tool list see it, but calling it there ends nothing.
The tool appears only when all of the following are true:
Model
: the session’s model is Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Fable 5, or a later version of one of those families.
Surface
: an interactive terminal session, including a
claude
session in an IDE’s integrated terminal, which is how the
JetBrains plugin
runs it. Other surfaces don’t include the tool, such as:
non-interactive
-p
runs
sessions through the
Agent SDK
TypeScript and Python packages
the
VS Code extension
panel, which bundles its own CLI
GitHub Actions
cloud sessions
Startup mode
: not a
--bare
session. Bare mode loads only shell and file tools, so the tool is never registered there.
Provider
: not available on
Amazon Bedrock
,
Claude Platform on AWS
,
Google Cloud’s Agent Platform
, or
Microsoft Foundry
, or on sessions signed in through a
cloud gateway
.
#### EnterWorktree tool behavior
The EnterWorktree tool creates an isolated
git worktree
and switches into it. Given a
path
, it switches into an existing worktree instead of creating a new one.
Which worktrees
path
can name
: on first entry the target may be a worktree of the current repository. In a repository that holds other repositories, it may also be a worktree of a repository nested inside it.
When you’re prompted
: a
path
outside
.claude/worktrees/
prompts for your approval before entering, since it moves the session’s working directory and write access to that location. New-worktree creation and paths under
.claude/worktrees/
don’t prompt. Before v2.1.206, Claude entered paths outside
.claude/worktrees/
without a prompt.
From inside a worktree
: from within a worktree session, only the
path
form is available and the target must be under
.claude/worktrees/
of the session’s repository. The same holds for a subagent with a pinned working directory, such as
isolation: worktree
.
When the tool is missing
: once
permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories
is on, Claude Code removes
EnterWorktree
and
ExitWorktree
or refuses calls to them. To keep working in worktrees, see
Claude has no
EnterWorktree
tool
.
#### Glob tool behavior
The Glob tool finds files by name pattern. On Windows, it’s part of the default tool set. On macOS, Linux, and WSL, Claude Code leaves Glob and
Grep
out of the default tool set, and Claude searches with
find
and
grep
through the Bash tool instead. In Claude’s shell those two commands run embedded versions of
bfs
and
ugrep
, and the searches reach your hooks and permission rules as
Bash
calls.
On macOS, Linux, and WSL, you get the Glob and Grep tools back in these cases:
You name
Glob
or
Grep
in
--tools
or
--allowedTools
when you start the session, or in the equivalent
Agent SDK
options. With
--tools
you get the ones you list, and naming either tool in
--allowedTools
restores both. An allow rule in a settings file doesn’t have this effect.
A permissions
deny rule
, the
--disallowedTools
flag, or
--restricted
removes
Bash
from the session.
A
subagent
lists
Glob
or
Grep
in its
tools
field and leaves out
Bash
. The listed tools come back for that subagent only, or for the whole session when it runs as the main session agent through
--agent
or the
agent
setting.
Glob supports standard glob syntax including
**
for recursive directory matching:
**/*.js
matches all
.js
files at any depth
src/**/*.ts
matches all
.ts
files under
src/
*.{json,yaml}
matches
.json
and
.yaml
files in the current directory
Results are sorted by modification time and capped at 100 files. If the cap is hit, Claude sees a truncation flag in the result and can narrow the pattern.
Glob doesn’t respect
.gitignore
by default, so it finds gitignored files alongside tracked ones. This differs from
Grep
, which skips gitignored files. To make Glob respect
.gitignore
, set
CLAUDE_CODE_GLOB_NO_IGNORE=false
before launching Claude Code.
Claude Code decides permission for a Glob call before it checks whether the search directory exists. It still runs the read-permission check for a missing
path
outside the
working directories
, so a permission prompt for a path doesn’t mean the path exists.
A
pattern
or
path
value that contains a null byte returns an error asking Claude to remove it.
#### Grep tool behavior
The Grep tool searches file contents for patterns. Where
Glob
finds files by name, Grep finds lines inside them. On macOS, Linux, and WSL, Grep is absent by default under the same conditions as Glob. See
Glob tool behavior
for when both tools are available.
Grep is built on
ripgrep
and uses ripgrep’s regex syntax, not POSIX grep. Patterns that include regex metacharacters need escaping. For example, finding
interface{}
in Go code takes the pattern
interface\{\}
.
A pattern, glob, or file type that ripgrep rejects returns an error that includes ripgrep’s diagnostic, so Claude can correct the input and search again. Before v2.1.208, Claude Code reported a rejected input as
No files found
instead of an error, even when the searched-for text existed in the target files.
Three output modes control what comes back:
files_with_matches
: file paths only, no line content. This is the default.
content
: matching lines with file and line number. When the tool’s
offset
parameter points past the last match for a pattern that has matches, Grep returns
No entries at this offset
, so Claude widens or resets the offset instead of concluding the pattern doesn’t match.
count
: match count per file, followed by a total across all matching files. The total covers every match even when the tool’s
head_limit
or
offset
parameters truncate the listed per-file entries.
Claude can scope results by file with the
glob
parameter, such as
**/*.tsx
, or by language with the
type
parameter, such as
py
or
rust
. By default, patterns match within a single line. Claude can set
multiline: true
to match across line boundaries.
Grep respects
.gitignore
, so gitignored files are skipped. To search a gitignored file, Claude passes its path directly.
Claude Code decides permission for a Grep call before it checks whether the search
path
exists. It still runs the read-permission check for a missing
path
outside the
working directories
, so a permission prompt for a path doesn’t mean the path exists.
#### LSP tool behavior
The LSP tool gives Claude code intelligence from a running language server. After each file edit, it automatically reports type errors and warnings so Claude can fix issues without a separate build step. Claude can also call it directly to navigate code:
Jump to a symbol’s definition
Find all references to a symbol
Get type information at a position
List symbols in a file
Search for a symbol by name across the workspace
Find implementations of an interface
Trace call hierarchies
Claude Code keeps the tool inactive until you install a
code intelligence plugin
for your language. In
cloud sessions
, Claude Code doesn’t start plugin language servers, so the LSP tool stays inactive there. Claude Code takes the language server’s configuration from the plugin, and you install the server binary yourself.
Claude Code returns an error result for each LSP call on a file whose language server it can’t start.
#### Monitor tool
The Monitor tool lets Claude watch something in the background and react when it changes, without pausing the conversation. Ask Claude to:
Tail a log file and flag errors as they appear
Poll a PR or CI job and report when its status changes
Watch a directory for file changes
Track output from any long-running script you point it at
Connect to a WebSocket feed and report each message as it arrives
For most watches, Claude writes a small script, runs it in the background, and receives each output line as it arrives. For a server that already pushes events, Claude can open a
WebSocket
instead of running a script.
Every watch Claude starts has a deadline: 5 minutes by default, at most 30 minutes, and at most 10 minutes in a
non-interactive
run given a single prompt with
-p
.
At the deadline the watch ends. Claude gets one notice, so it can start the watch again if it’s still needed.
Stop a monitor by asking Claude to cancel it or by ending the session. When you stop a
subagent
that started monitors, for example from
/tasks
, those monitors stop with it.
When Monitor runs a command, it uses the same
permission rules as Bash
, so
allow
and
deny
patterns you have set for Bash apply here too. While
auto mode
is active, Claude Code sets aside allow rules that name
Monitor
itself, along with the other
broad allow rules it drops
, so the classifier reviews Monitor commands the same way it reviews Bash commands.
Monitor needs a minimum version or Git Bash in these cases:
Minimum version
: on Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry, or with
DISABLE_TELEMETRY
or
CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC
set, Monitor requires Claude Code v2.1.310 or later. The requirement applies when
feature-flag fetching
is off
Windows
: the tool is available only when
Git Bash
is installed
Plugins can declare monitors that start automatically when the plugin is active, instead of asking Claude to start them. See
plugin monitors
.
##### WebSocket source
When a server already pushes events over a WebSocket, Claude can connect to it directly instead of writing a polling script. Each kind of socket activity either becomes an event or ends the watch:
Text messages
: each one becomes one event, even when the message spans multiple lines.
Binary messages
: not passed through. Claude receives a placeholder line such as
[binary frame, 512 bytes]
instead.
Messages larger than 1 MiB
: the watch ends, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.
Socket close
: the watch ends and Claude receives the close code.
A WebSocket watch takes a
ws
input in place of
command
, and a single Monitor call can’t combine the two. The
ws
input has two fields:
Field
Required
Description
url
Yes
The endpoint to connect to. Must be a
ws://
or
wss://
URL with no embedded credentials or whitespace, using ASCII characters only
protocols
No
WebSocket subprotocol names to offer during the handshake. Each entry must be a valid subprotocol token, and the list can’t contain duplicates
The
timeout_ms
deadline applies to a WebSocket watch too: the watch ends at the deadline, and
TaskStop
cancels it early.
Without a
Monitor
allow rule, you’re prompted before Claude opens a WebSocket; in
auto mode
the classifier decides instead, unless an
ask rule
applies. The prompt doesn’t offer an option to skip future prompts for the same host.
###### Addresses and hosts denied to WebSocket watches
Claude Code denies URLs that point at a private, link-local, or cloud-metadata address, including hostnames that your machine resolves to one. Behind a
proxy
, a watch can reach a private, link-local, or cloud-metadata address unless the proxy blocks it, because Claude Code doesn’t check the address the proxy finds. Claude Code also denies hosts in
sandbox.network.deniedDomains
, and when
allowManagedDomainsOnly
is set in managed settings, any host outside the managed allowlist.
If a watch behind a proxy fails with
could not resolve <host>
, restart Claude Code v2.1.319 or later with
CLAUDE_CODE_PROXY_RESOLVES_HOSTS
set to
1
so the proxy looks up the hostname.
###### Bash rules that deny or prompt for WebSocket watches
If Claude Code refuses a
Monitor
call that opens a WebSocket, look for a
deny or ask rule
written
Bash
or
Bash(*)
. Do the same if it prompts for that call despite your
Monitor
allow rule. A rule on every Bash command also covers these WebSocket watches:
Deny rule
: if the rule is in place when the session starts, Claude doesn’t have the Monitor tool, so it can’t start the watch. If you add the rule during a session, Claude’s next
Monitor
call is refused. The refusal reads
Permission to use Monitor has been denied: it runs code as Bash does, and a rule denies Bash.
Ask rule
: you’re asked to approve the watch. You can’t have an allow rule, a
PreToolUse
hook,
bypassPermissions
mode, or the auto mode classifier approve it for you. You can approve it from a
PermissionRequest
hook
. Where nobody can answer, such as in
dontAsk
mode, Claude Code denies the watch.
To let these watches run, narrow the rule to the commands you mean, such as
Bash(rm *)
.
The ask rule, and a deny rule you add during a session, cover these watches in Claude Code v2.1.319 or later.
#### NotebookEdit tool behavior
NotebookEdit modifies a Jupyter notebook one cell at a time, targeting cells by their
cell_id
. It doesn’t perform string replacement across the notebook the way
Edit
does on plain files.
Three edit modes control what happens to the target cell:
replace
: overwrite the cell’s source. This is the default.
insert
: add a new cell after the target. With no
cell_id
, the new cell goes at the start of the notebook. Requires
cell_type
set to
code
or
markdown
.
delete
: remove the target cell.
NotebookEdit refuses a notebook file that doesn’t decode as UTF-8, under the
same rule as Edit
, and writes nothing.
Permission rules use the
Edit(...)
path format. A rule like
Edit(notebooks/**)
covers NotebookEdit calls on files in that directory.
##### Replacing a cell clears its saved outputs in the file
When NotebookEdit replaces a code cell, its execution count and saved outputs are cleared. To get the output back, re-run the cell and any cells that use the functions or variables it defines. See
Work with Jupyter notebooks
for the VS Code workflow.
#### PowerShell tool
The PowerShell tool lets Claude run PowerShell commands natively. On Windows, this means commands run in PowerShell instead of routing through Git Bash. How the tool becomes available depends on your platform:
Windows without Git Bash
: the tool is enabled automatically.
Windows with Git Bash installed
: the tool is on by default for claude.ai and Console accounts; set
CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1
to enable it in Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry sessions, or
0
to turn it off.
Linux, macOS, and WSL
: the tool is opt-in.
Your
PreToolUse hooks
receive the tool’s command string in
tool_input.command
, with the same fields as the Bash tool.
Match
Bash|PowerShell
in hooks that inspect shell commands; the
PowerShell hook input section
explains why matching
Bash
alone is not enough.
##### Enable the PowerShell tool
Set
CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1
in your environment or in
settings.json
:
{
"env"
: {
"CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL"
:
"1"
}
}
On Windows, set the variable to
0
to turn the tool off. On Linux, macOS, and WSL, the tool requires PowerShell 7 or later: install
pwsh
and ensure it is on your
PATH
.
On Windows, Claude Code auto-detects
pwsh.exe
for PowerShell 7+ with a fallback to
powershell.exe
for PowerShell 5.1. When the tool is enabled, Claude treats PowerShell as the primary shell. The Bash tool remains available for POSIX scripts when Git Bash is installed.
Claude Code spawns PowerShell with
-ExecutionPolicy Bypass
at process scope only, so
.ps1
scripts and module imports work on default Windows installs without changing the machine’s policy. Process-scope bypass doesn’t override Group Policy
MachinePolicy
or
UserPolicy
, so enterprise policies still apply. To respect the machine’s effective execution policy instead, set
CLAUDE_CODE_POWERSHELL_RESPECT_EXECUTION_POLICY=1
.
##### Bash deny rules also turn off the PowerShell tool
On Windows with Git Bash installed, denying Bash also turns the PowerShell tool off for the session. This applies to scoped rules such as
Bash(git push *)
as well as a bare
Bash
, and to rules from one of your settings files or
--disallowedTools
. Claude Code does this because a
Bash
rule doesn’t restrict the PowerShell tool, which has
its own permission rules
. With PowerShell left on, Claude could run there what your rule denies in Bash.
To keep the PowerShell tool on alongside a Bash deny rule, do either of these:
Set
CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1
in your environment or in the
env
block of a settings file, as shown in
Enable the PowerShell tool
.
Add a scoped
PowerShell
permission rule
to a settings file, such as a
PowerShell(git push *)
deny rule.
Without one of these, a scoped Bash deny rule leaves the Bash tool available, and Claude Code turns PowerShell off without a warning. A rule that removes the whole Bash tool leaves Claude with no shell tool for the session.
##### Shell selection in settings, hooks, and skills
Three additional settings control where PowerShell is used:
"defaultShell": "powershell"
in
settings.json
: routes interactive
!
commands through PowerShell. Requires the PowerShell tool to be enabled.
"shell": "powershell"
on individual
command hooks
: runs that hook in PowerShell. Hooks spawn PowerShell directly, so this works regardless of
CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL
.
shell: powershell
in
skill frontmatter
: runs
!`command`
blocks in PowerShell. Requires the PowerShell tool to be enabled.
PowerShell commands follow the
same main-session working-directory reset behavior
as Bash commands, including the
CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR
environment variable.
PowerShell commands also receive the variables hooks persist through
CLAUDE_ENV_FILE
, under the conditions in
Persisted variables in PowerShell commands
. Requires Claude Code v2.1.296 or later.
##### Exit code 1 from searches and git diff in PowerShell
If a
grep
or
rg
search that matches nothing shows
Error: Exit code 1
when Claude runs it in the PowerShell tool, the search didn’t fail. You don’t need to do anything. The error can appear when the search is part of a longer command. For example, when
rg
exits with code 1,
rg foo | Out-Null
shows the error and
rg foo
doesn’t.
The PowerShell tool can count exit code 1 as a normal result from
grep
,
rg
,
egrep
,
fgrep
,
findstr
,
git grep
, and
git diff
. The searches use exit code 1 to report no matches. From
git diff
, exit code 1 means the files differ. A command that shows the error when Claude runs it
counts as failed
in a skill with
shell: powershell
.
##### Windows encoding and exit codes
Redirection with
>
and
>>
writes UTF-8 files on PowerShell 5.1
Claude Code encodes text piped to a native command’s standard input as UTF-8
Claude Code captures error output without ANSI escape sequences
A command whose child process waits on standard input receives end-of-file instead of hanging
If
where.exe
finds no match, or
fc.exe
or
diff.exe
finds that the files differ, the result can show
Error: Exit code 1
though the command didn’t fail. You don’t need to do anything.
If a
robocopy
exit code from 1 through 7 shows as an error, the copy didn’t fail and you don’t need to do anything.
robocopy
exits with code 0 through 7 to report a result, such as files copied, and with 8 or higher when it fails.
##### Preview limitations
The PowerShell tool has the following known limitations during the preview:
PowerShell profiles are not loaded
On Windows, sandboxing is not supported
#### Read tool behavior
The Read tool takes a file path and returns the contents with line numbers.
Reading an empty file returns a notice that the file exists but its contents are empty, and an
offset
past the last line returns a notice giving the file’s line count.
Read handles several file types beyond plain text:
Images
: PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP files are returned as visual content that Claude can see, not as raw bytes. Claude Code resizes and recompresses large images to fit the model’s image size limits before sending them, so Claude may see a downscaled version of a large screenshot.
If Claude misses fine pixel-level detail in a large image, ask it to crop the region you care about, such as with ImageMagick via Bash, and then read the crop.
Read refuses an image file larger than 128 MB with an error that tells Claude to resize the image or export a smaller copy, then read that copy. If Claude stops at the error instead of doing so, see
File is too large to read as an image
.
PDFs
: Claude reads short
.pdf
files whole. For PDFs longer than 10 pages, it reads in ranges with a
pages
parameter, such as
"1-5"
, up to 20 pages at a time. Page-range reads render pages with
pdftoppm
from poppler-utils, so install it with
brew install poppler
on macOS or
apt-get install poppler-utils
on Debian and Ubuntu. On Windows and other platforms, install a poppler build that puts
pdftoppm
on your
PATH
. Without it, a page-range read fails with
pdftoppm is not installed
.
Jupyter notebooks
:
.ipynb
files return all cells with their outputs, including code, markdown, and visualizations. A notebook whose cells come to more than 256 KB, or more than the
token limit
, returns an error instead. Claude Code refuses to read a notebook file over 100 MB; the error tells Claude how to read a portion of the notebook instead, such as a slice of cells, with a shell command.
Read only reads files, not directories. Claude lists directory contents with a shell command such as
ls
.
Read refuses a file whose extension it treats as binary, such as
.xlsx
,
.parquet
,
.heic
, or
.zip
. Claude keeps working after a refusal: the error suggests a skill for that file type if one is available, or else a shell command or script that reads the format. If you
@
-mention
a file that Read refuses, Claude receives the file’s path but not its contents.
##### Large files
Claude can read a text file larger than a single Read call returns. By default one call returns at most 25,000 tokens, or the value you set in
CLAUDE_CODE_FILE_READ_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS
, and refuses a whole file over 256 KB, so Claude reads a larger file in pages with
offset
and
limit
. On Claude Code v2.1.296 or later it can instead read the whole file, or a long line range, in one call by setting
allow_large: true
when it needs to, for example because you asked for the entire file. That read is sized against the room left in the session’s
context window
instead of the default limits. Images, PDFs, and notebooks keep their limits.
What Claude receives when a read goes over the default limits:
Whole file over the token limit
: the first page of the file, with a
PARTIAL view
notice saying how much of the file it received and how to read more with
offset
and
limit
Whole file over 256 KB, or an
offset
or
limit
read over the token limit
: an error telling it to read a portion with
offset
and
limit
, or to search for specific content with
Grep
instead
#### SendFeedback tool behavior
Claude-drafted feedback is a feedback report about Claude Code that Claude writes for you. It requires Claude Code v2.1.238 or later. Claude Code saves each draft on your machine under
~/.claude/feedback/drafts/
, and nothing reaches Anthropic until you send it. Claude drafts one with the SendFeedback tool when:
A tool or command keeps failing
It can’t help with something you asked for
You point out a mistake it made, or it notices one
You ask it to file feedback
##### What you see when Claude drafts
After Claude queues a draft, you see a card above your prompt with the draft’s title. Press
1
to review the draft, press
2
twice to send it as written, or press
0
to dismiss it. A dismissed draft stays in your queue. After you dismiss a card, Claude Code asks whether to turn Claude-drafted feedback off. It stops asking once you’ve declined twice.
By default, you see at most three cards in a session; Anthropic can adjust that limit from the server without a release. After the limit, and whenever you set
feedbackDrafts
to
quiet
, you see only a count of queued drafts in the prompt footer.
##### Review and edit a draft
Run
/feedback
with no argument to open your queue. It lists every queued draft from all your sessions, including drafts whose cards you dismissed or never saw. Select a draft to open it for review, where you can:
Edit the title, area, and details
Set
Send transcript
to
yes
or
no
. When the transcript from the session where Claude queued the draft is still available, it starts at
yes
, which sends that conversation to Anthropic;
no
sends the report only
Send the draft, discard it, or leave it in the queue for later
To write a report yourself instead, press
w
for the standard feedback dialog.
/feedback
with text after it, and
/bug
, open that dialog directly.
##### Send a draft
When you send a draft, Claude Code submits it the same way as a
/feedback
report, with the same
retention
, and deletes the draft from your machine. When you send from the card, it shows
✓ Sent
; when you send from the queue, it closes with a receipt ID.
The report carries:
Your title, area, and details
Environment info, such as your Claude Code version, operating system, and model
The IDs of recent API requests
The conversation transcript, when you left
Send transcript
at
yes
in the review screen. Sending from the card never includes the transcript
Claude Code keeps your working directory in the local draft so it can find the transcript, and doesn’t send the directory.
In
organizations with Zero Data Retention
, and in organizations with the
HIPAA configuration
applied, Claude Code leaves the SendFeedback tool out of your sessions. If a session in an organization with Zero Data Retention still offers the tool, drafts stay on your machine, and sending fails with
Feedback collection is not available for organizations with custom data retention policies.
##### Discard or keep a draft
When you discard a draft, Claude Code deletes it from your machine. A draft you leave in the queue expires after 30 days, or after
cleanupPeriodDays
when that’s shorter. The queue holds 10 drafts across all your sessions, and when Claude queues an eleventh, Claude Code deletes the oldest. When you run
/exit
with drafts from the session still in the queue, Claude Code asks whether to review them or discard them before exiting.
##### Turn Claude-drafted feedback off
Set
Claude-drafted feedback
to
off
in
/config
, which writes the
feedbackDrafts
setting, or set
CLAUDE_CODE_SEND_FEEDBACK=0
for one session. With either, Claude can’t queue drafts. To keep drafting on without cards, set
feedbackDrafts
to
quiet
instead. Administrators can set
feedbackDrafts
in
managed settings
, which takes precedence over your own setting.
##### Sessions without Claude-drafted feedback
Claude Code includes the tool in interactive terminal sessions on your own machine that use the Claude API rather than a cloud provider. It leaves the tool out of:
Non-interactive
-p
runs and
Agent SDK
sessions, which have no screen to review the queue on
Cloud sessions
, which can’t write to the queue on your machine
Sessions on
Amazon Bedrock
,
Claude Platform on AWS
,
Google Cloud’s Agent Platform
, or
Microsoft Foundry
Sessions that reach Claude through an
LLM gateway
with the gateway’s own key or token
Sessions where you set
CLAUDE_CODE_SEND_FEEDBACK=0
or
DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND=1
, set
CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC
to any non-empty value, or turned off
feature-flag fetching
Organizations that have turned off product feedback,
organizations with Zero Data Retention
, and organizations with the
HIPAA configuration
applied
Sessions where Claude Code has
stopped offering feedback after a refused report
#### Task tool availability
The task-tracking tools,
TaskCreate
,
TaskGet
,
TaskUpdate
,
TaskList
, and
TodoWrite
, are available by default only on Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5, and earlier models. Wherever the tools are available, you get the four Task tools, or
TodoWrite
instead when you set
CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=0
.
On every other model, Claude Code leaves the tools out unless you opt in. The same applies to a model ID Claude Code doesn’t recognize, such as a custom model name served through an
LLM gateway
. On newer models, Claude keeps track of multi-step work without a written checklist, and the tools’ definitions and reminders take up context. Without the tools, Claude adds nothing to the
task list
while it works.
If you’d like to use these tools on a model that doesn’t have them by default, do one of the following:
Export
CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1
before you start Claude Code, for example
CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 claude
. Claude Code then provides the same tools on every model and every provider
Name one of the tools in
--allowedTools
, for example
claude --allowedTools TaskCreate
List the tools in
--tools
, which restricts the session’s built-in tools to the ones it names. Include the tools you want alongside the other built-in tools you use
In the Agent SDK, the
allowedTools
and
tools
options
work the same way as the two flags
In
background sessions
and in
cloud sessions
, Claude Code provides the same tools on every model, listed or not.
The default set described here applies in Claude Code v2.1.268 and later.
##### Task-tracking tools in subagents and agent teams
A subagent has the task-tracking tools only when your session has them, whatever model the subagent runs. An in-process
agent team
teammate has the task-tracking tools when your session does. A
split-pane
teammate is a separate Claude Code process that
inherits
your
--tools
list and deny rules, not
--allowedTools
, so check what you set:
No
--tools
list or deny rule, and
CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS
unset for the teammate
: the teammate has the task-tracking tools its own model has by default.
CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS
exported in your shell
: Claude Code passes the teammate a fixed set of environment variables that doesn’t include the one you exported. To set it for the teammate too, start your session by running
claude --settings '{"env":{"CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS":"1"}}'
in your shell. The teammate also gets your
--settings
value.
--tools
naming the task-tracking tools
: the teammate has them on any model.
A task-tracking tool missing from
--tools
or named in a deny rule
: the teammate lacks that tool.
Without the Task tools, an agent coordinates with its team through messages instead of the
shared task list
.
#### WebFetch tool behavior
Claude uses WebFetch to look something up on a web page. The URL can come from you or from Claude, for example from a
WebSearch
result. For most pages, Claude doesn’t see the full text. It asks a question about the page, and a separate model call reads the page and returns an answer.
##### Allow a domain
Terminal and VS Code sessions
start in auto mode by default
. In auto mode, you don’t see a prompt before a fetch, except for a domain that an
ask
rule matches. The
classifier
reviews the fetch instead and can block it. In Manual and
acceptEdits
modes, Claude Code asks for your permission.
To approve a domain ahead of time, add an allow rule to a
settings file
, or select
Yes, and don’t ask again for
<domain>
when a prompt offers it. This example allows
example.com
:
{
"permissions"
: {
"allow"
: [
"WebFetch(domain:example.com)"
]
}
}
To confirm, run
/permissions
in a session. The dialog lists the rule. Select it to see which settings it comes from.
To allow
Use this rule
One domain
WebFetch(domain:example.com)
Its subdomains
WebFetch(domain:*.example.com)
Every site
WebFetch
or
WebFetch(domain:*)
. See
how the two differ
.
With a
domain:
allow rule,
sandboxed Bash commands
can also reach the domain, unless a
sandbox lock
makes the sandbox ignore the rule.
##### Block a site or turn WebFetch off
To
Do this
Block a domain
Add a
WebFetch(domain:...)
rule for it to
deny
Require a prompt for a domain
Add a
WebFetch(domain:...)
rule for it to
ask
Turn WebFetch off
Add
WebFetch
to
deny
, or set
CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WEB_FETCH
to
1
Do any of these for your organization
Put the rule in
managed settings
Outside the sandbox, if Bash is allowed, Claude can still use
curl
,
wget
, or other tools to reach any URL. See
Tool-specific permission rules
.
##### When a fetch prompts, fails, or WebFetch is missing
Claude’s reply can leave out anything on the page that Claude didn’t ask about. In the terminal, press
Ctrl+O
to see what Claude asked and the answer it received.
What you notice
What to do
Claude says a page doesn’t cover something you know is there
Ask Claude to fetch the page again and tell it what to look for. For the raw page, ask it to run
curl
on the URL through the Bash tool.
Claude leaves out the end of a long page, or says part of it wasn’t read
Ask Claude to fetch the next part of the page. This requires Claude Code v2.1.290 or later. The
web-fetch
subagent
reads pages of up to about 48,000 characters in full, and WebFetch reads the first 100,000 when Claude calls it.
Claude describes a page as it was before a recent change
WebFetch reuses its copy of a page for 15 minutes. To change how long, set
CLAUDE_CODE_WEBFETCH_CACHE_TTL_MS
.
Claude says the download ran out of time
A download fails after five minutes. To change the limit, set
CLAUDE_CODE_WEBFETCH_DEADLINE_MS
.
Claude reports a redirect and stops there
Ask Claude to fetch the new URL. When a redirect changes the host by more than adding or dropping
www.
, WebFetch returns the new URL and no page content.
Claude can’t fetch a local or intranet server
WebFetch
refuses
localhost
and any other hostname without a dot. Ask Claude to reach the server with
curl
through the Bash tool.
In a cloud session, Claude says the network blocks the domain
An allow rule isn’t enough there. Also
add the domain
to the cloud environment’s network access.
In auto mode, a fetch is blocked and you see no prompt
Add an allow rule for the domain. If the classifier blocked the fetch, you can also open
/permissions
in the terminal and
approve the fetch
under the
Recently blocked
tab so Claude can retry.
In
claude -p
or the Agent SDK, a fetch is denied
These runs
start in Manual mode
, and a call that needs approval is denied. Add an allow rule or start in auto mode.
A fetch fails for a domain you allowed
The URL also has to pass the
WebFetch domain safety check
, unless you turn the check off with
skipWebFetchPreflight
. See
WebFetch domain safety check failed
.
A rule in your own settings file has no effect
If your organization sets
allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly
, Claude Code ignores the rule. Ask your administrator to add it to managed settings.
Prompts continue after you add the domain to the sandbox’s
allowedDomains
WebFetch doesn’t read that list, so add a WebFetch allow rule
No prompt for a domain you didn’t allow
Claude Code skips the prompt for a built-in set of preapproved documentation domains, and in
auto
and
bypassPermissions
modes. To require the prompt anyway, add an
ask
rule for the domain. Sandboxed Bash commands don’t inherit the preapproved set.
A claude.ai artifact link brings another prompt
See
Read an artifact shared with you
Claude can’t fetch any page
Run
/status
in the session. If the
Organization configuration
line lists
HIPAA
, WebFetch is off: see
What developers see in Claude Code
. If the
Organization policy
line reports that the policy didn’t load and names web fetch, follow any fix the line names. WebFetch becomes available again without a restart once a policy that allows it loads.
##### The web-fetch subagent
web-fetch
is the
subagent
built into Claude Code that reads web pages for Claude. When Claude needs a page, it calls the
Agent tool
to pass
web-fetch
the URL and a question about the page. The subagent calls WebFetch, reads the page, and sends Claude the answer.
Your session can use the subagent when you’re signed in with a claude.ai account on Claude Code v2.1.287 or later. Without it, Claude calls WebFetch itself, and the model that Claude Code uses for
background tasks
reads the page. The subagent is off in setups such as these:
You
turned the subagent off
You connect through an
LLM gateway
on Claude Code v2.1.330 or later
Claude Code
doesn’t fetch feature flags
, such as on Amazon Bedrock or with
DISABLE_TELEMETRY
set
These signs mean the subagent fetched a page:
Terminal
: the permission prompt’s title is
Fetch · from the web-fetch agent
. The line that starts with
Received
shows only a size, such as
Received 87 bytes
.
VS Code
: the fetch appears as an
Agent
row
Desktop app or claude.ai/code
: the fetch appears as a row that opens a subagent pane
claude -p
or the Agent SDK
: in the
system/init
event
,
agents
lists
web-fetch
and
tools
doesn’t list
WebFetch
###### Which model the web-fetch subagent runs on
By default, the
web-fetch
subagent runs on the model that the
haiku
model alias
points to. If the subagent can’t use that model, such as when your
availableModels
allowlist leaves it out, it runs on the same model as the conversation that started it. To choose the model yourself,
run every subagent on one model
.
###### Rules, hooks, and CLAUDE.md with the web-fetch subagent
Your
WebFetch
permission rules
apply to the pages the
web-fetch
subagent fetches, and so do the
PreToolUse
and
PostToolUse
hooks
that match
WebFetch
.
If you rely on
With the subagent
What to do
CLAUDE.md instructions about which pages to fetch
The subagent starts without your CLAUDE.md files, including your organization’s managed one
Restrict fetches with
WebFetch
permission rules
SubagentStart
or
SubagentStop
hooks
Only the hooks defined in
managed settings
run for this subagent
In any other settings file, use a
PreToolUse
or
PostToolUse
hook that matches
WebFetch
A
PostToolUse
hook that parses the
WebFetch
result
The result is the page text. When Claude calls WebFetch itself, the result is an answer to Claude’s question.
Handle both page text and answers in the hook
A
PreToolUse
hook that blocks
Agent
calls
Claude starts the subagent with the
Agent
tool, so the page isn’t fetched
Turn the subagent off
###### Turn off the web-fetch subagent
Turn the
web-fetch
subagent off when your setup depends on Claude calling WebFetch itself, for example when a
PreToolUse
hook blocks every
Agent
call. Add this
deny rule
to a
settings file
, or to managed settings to cover your organization:
{
"permissions"
: {
"deny"
: [
"Agent(web-fetch)"
]
}
}
To confirm, start a new session, ask Claude to fetch a page, and check that the
signs of the subagent
don’t appear. In the
system/init
event,
tools
lists
WebFetch
again and
agents
still lists
web-fetch
.
If your organization sets
allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly
, Claude Code ignores the deny rule in your own settings files, so ask your administrator to add it to managed settings.
##### Identify WebFetch requests to your site
WebFetch sets a
User-Agent
header beginning with
Claude-User
, and an
Accept
header that prefers Markdown over HTML so servers that support content negotiation can return Markdown directly.
#### WebSearch tool behavior
WebSearch runs a query against Anthropic’s
web search
backend and returns result titles and URLs. It doesn’t fetch the result pages. To read a page Claude finds in search results, it follows up with
WebFetch
.
The tool may issue up to eight backend searches per call. Claude can scope results with
allowed_domains
to include only certain hosts, or
blocked_domains
to exclude them. The two lists can’t be combined in a single call.
When the search request hits an overloaded API, Claude Code retries it with backoff; a call that still fails returns an error result.
WebSearch permission rules take no specifier. A bare
WebSearch
entry in
allow
or
deny
is the only form.
The search backend is not configurable. To search with a different provider, add an
MCP server
that exposes a search tool.
WebSearch is available on the Claude API,
Claude Platform on AWS
,
Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)
, and Microsoft Foundry. On Google Cloud’s Agent Platform it works with Opus 4, Sonnet 4, Haiku 4.5, and later models. Amazon Bedrock doesn’t expose the server-side web search tool.
##### Session search limit
An interactive terminal session has a limit of 200 WebSearch calls. Searches from the main conversation and from
subagents
, such as a parallel research fan-out, count against the same limit.
While a session is at the limit, searches appear in the conversation as calls that did nothing. Claude gets a notice telling it to continue with the information already gathered, say so in its answer, and, if it needs more searches, ask you to raise the limit.
To get more searches, raise the cap, wait for the limit to refill, or start a new conversation:
Raise the cap
: set the
CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION
environment variable to a positive whole number, such as
500
. The cap can be raised but not turned off.
Wait for the refill
: on Claude Code v2.1.290 or later, an interactive terminal session’s limit refills at about 100 calls per hour. To change the rate, set
CLAUDE_CODE_WEB_SEARCH_REFILLS_PER_HOUR
to a number of calls per hour, such as
50
.
Start a new conversation
: running
/clear
at the Claude Code prompt also resets the count. If work that can still spawn subagents survives the clear, such as a running workflow, the count carries over instead.
In
non-interactive mode
with
-p
and in the
Agent SDK
, the limit applies per turn, not per session. A turn lasts from a message you send until Claude finishes responding. The limit resets when you send the next message after that or start a new
claude -p
run, even with
--continue
or
--resume
. For more searches, raise
CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION
or set a refill rate with
CLAUDE_CODE_WEB_SEARCH_REFILLS_PER_HOUR
.
#### Write tool behavior
The Write tool creates a new file or overwrites an existing one with the full content provided. It doesn’t append or merge. Write also overwrites an existing file whose bytes don’t decode and saves the new content as UTF-8, as described under
non-UTF-8 files
.
Whether Claude must read an existing file in the current conversation before overwriting it depends on the model and the file:
Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Haiku 4.5, and older models always require the read, so a Write to an unread existing file fails with an error.
Newer models can overwrite a file they never read this session under the same conditions as
read-before-edit
: reading it wouldn’t need a permission prompt and the Read tool is available.
Jupyter notebooks, and files Claude has read only partially with a
PARTIAL view
notice
, require the read on every model.
This constraint doesn’t apply to new files.
Viewing the file with Bash also satisfies this requirement under the same rules described in
Edit tool behavior
.
For partial changes to an existing file, Claude uses Edit instead of Write.
#### Check which tools are available
Your exact tool set depends on your provider, platform, and settings. To check what’s loaded in a running session, ask Claude directly:
What tools do you have access to?
Claude gives a conversational summary. For exact MCP tool names, run
/mcp
.
The
advisor tool
is a
server tool
that the API runs, rather than a tool that Claude Code implements. It has no name you can reference in permission rules or hook matchers.
#### See also
MCP servers
: add custom tools by connecting external servers
Permissions
: permission system, rule syntax, and tool-specific patterns
Subagents
: configure tool access for subagents
Hooks
: run custom commands before or after tool execution

## Source (changelog): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md

### Changelog

#### 2.1.330

- Added sign-in to organizations managed in Anthropic's Enterprise Admin Console: after `claude auth login`, Claude Code applies the organization's settings and uses its cloud provider or gateway
- Added easel, a built-in mod that draws charts when asked and under MCP metrics results, on Pro, Max and, where available, Team and Enterprise on macOS and Linux; turn automatic charts off in `/config`
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_FULL_SIGN_IN_LINK=1` to print the full sign-in link, if the short one shows an error or a script reads values from it
- Self-hosted runner: Added `--start-dir` / `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_START_DIR` to have Claude start its work in a folder of a repository, while settings and hooks load as without it
- Added a notice in cloud and self-hosted runner sessions when a plugin marketplace can't be fetched because its repository isn't one of the session's
- Self-hosted runner: Added a notice when Anthropic-managed git refuses a plugin's own repository, naming the plugin and what to do
- Added `commandPrinted` to `claude plugin install --json` results, true when the plugin's install command wrote to stderr, and `commandFailed` when it exited with an error, was killed or timed out
- Added `claude_code_self_hosted_runner_order_to_registered_seconds` to the self-hosted runner's `/metrics`: seconds from work order issued to registration accepted, on orchestrator-spawned runners
- Added `claude_code_self_hosted_runner_order_to_first_session_seconds` to the self-hosted runner's `/metrics`: seconds from work order to first session handed over, on runners started for a session
- Fixed Claude Code freezing for up to several minutes right after compacting a very long conversation
- Fixed WebFetch freezing the session for minutes on some pages, and returning an empty result for some others
- Fixed `ExitWorktree` and the worktree exit dialog deleting a worktree that another running Claude Code session was working in
- Fixed changes to user settings being lost when several Claude Code processes saved them at the same time
- Fixed `--continue` and `--resume` opening an empty session or failing when the last saved message had a missing or invalid timestamp
- Fixed the first prompt after a sleep of two minutes or more waiting three minutes on a connection that had died, on Linux and WSL
- Fixed turns failing with "JSON schema is invalid", and session files growing by many megabytes, when many MCP tools have an input schema that the API refuses
- Linux: Fixed Bash commands waiting seconds and showing no file diff for the rest of a session in slow repositories with large ignored folders such as `node_modules`
- Windows: Fixed Bash commands running slower for the rest of a session after Git Bash took 10 to 60 seconds to start, on machines with no custom start-up files
- Fixed `/rewind` sometimes restoring an older version of a file when two queued prompts, or stacked skills, ran together right after a turn that changed it
- Fixed text and images added when approving a permission prompt being dropped when the approved command or tool then failed
- Fixed MCP resources from claude.ai connectors and plugin servers not being attached when @-mentioned in the terminal's prompt box
- Fixed an MCP server that subagents declare being shut down when one of them finished, while other subagents or the session were still using it
- Fixed Claude in Chrome staying "not connected" after a brief connection problem, even though Chrome was open and signed in
- Fixed terminal sessions on Amazon Bedrock (Mantle) started with no model selected ignoring a pinned Opus model, and still calling an unavailable default model after announcing a fallback
- Fixed the rest of what you were typing being lost when a plan arrived in fullscreen mode
- Fixed claude.ai connectors with different names being dropped when they share a server URL (anthropics/claude-code#101856)
- Fixed plugins going missing from the installed list when several `claude plugin` commands ran at the same time
- Fixed task dependencies and metadata being lost when several task updates ran at the same time
- Fixed incomplete backups of `~/.claude.json` being kept, and displacing good ones, when the disk was full
- Fixed a long pause in Code Mode after code that read hundreds of files in projects with path-scoped rules or Read deny rules
- Fixed the built-in chart tool failing when Claude called it in Code Mode
- Fixed Code Mode ignoring an MCP tool's request to end the turn from a script in auto and bypass permissions modes
- Fixed Code Mode in auto mode dropping earlier thinking and rewriting the prompt cache when a mod added a note after a script loaded a skill
- Fixed Code Mode not restoring a file that a script had read after Esc and `/compact`
- Fixed `/context` undercounting system tools in Code Mode before Claude's first reply
- Fixed a stopped background subagent sometimes not staying stopped
- Fixed Claude still waiting for a background agent that was stopped just as it finished, in sessions run by an app or the SDK
- Fixed background sessions sometimes waking in their previous permission mode after approving a plan
- Remote Control: Fixed the note about background agents ended by a Stop from a phone or the web showing in the terminal as if you had typed it
- Remote Control: Fixed the mobile apps hiding the Diff and pull request buttons, or showing a stopped session as working, after turning it on mid-conversation
- Fixed environment variables written by a SessionStart hook being lost with `claude -p --continue`
- Fixed `claude -p` exiting 0 with no message when its output went to a file on a full disk: it now prints an error and exits 1, though a full NFS export may go unnoticed
- Fixed the system prompt keeping the earlier model's instructions when the model was changed after `/context` but before the first message
- Fixed Claude sometimes replying to its commit attribution reminder and ending the turn early after the model changed mid-turn; it can still happen where managed settings set the PR attribution line
- Fixed Esc not ending an LSP tool call that was waiting for a slow or stuck language server
- Fixed LSP tool calls and diagnostics failing when several calls or edits arrived while a language server was still starting
- Fixed `/mcp` listing plugin servers as built-in: they now stand under "Plugin MCPs", `--mcp-config` and built-in servers under "Other MCPs", and a server's page names its plugin
- Fixed an "MCP server blocked by enterprise policy: easel" warning showing at every start when an MCP allowlist or denylist excludes the built-in chart tool, which stays blocked
- Fixed `/stats` counting new activity in UTC days instead of your local time zone
- Fixed `/ultrareview` failing or reviewing the wrong code after the shell moved into another repository: it now stops and names both folders
- Fixed Grep reporting no matches when the pattern held a line break without multiline mode; it now reports the rejected pattern
- Fixed Jupyter notebooks saved with a byte order mark being reported as invalid JSON by the Read and NotebookEdit tools
- Fixed link reference definitions being dropped from CLAUDE.md and memory files that contain an HTML comment
- Fixed running Monitors keeping the earlier conversation in memory until they end
- Fixed some Claude Desktop sessions on third-party providers, other than scheduled tasks, ending a turn with "Prompt is too long" when a PDF larger than the context window followed a long conversation
- Fixed the choice between two user or project agent files declaring the same name depending on the order the file search listed them
- Fixed `claude daemon logs` never exiting inside a git repository when there is no log file
- Fixed markdown hiding a character or two after bold or italic text when a backslash came before an emoji later in the paragraph
- Fixed Edit refusing some valid hook commands in Claude settings files
- Fixed `Read` with a page range showing both halves of a scanned two-page spread on each of its pages
- Fixed line breaks and class stereotypes missing from Mermaid diagrams in HTML artifacts
- Fixed the Project instructions picker in `/config` showing only one of its four choices in a 24-row fullscreen window
- Fixed a subagent's own subagents and forks running on the plan-mode model in plan mode under `opusplan` or `haiku`
- Fixed WebFetch page summaries ignoring the `/effort` level when a gateway refuses the small fast model
- Fixed `claude -p` on Google Cloud's Agent Platform ignoring `--settings '{"fastMode":true}'` when the model comes from `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` or a settings file; such runs now bill at the fast mode price
- Fixed startup under `forceLoginOrgUUID` being refused after one temporary server error or dropped connection
- Fixed `claude mcp remove` giving no way forward for a claude.ai connector: it now says to turn it off in /mcp or remove it on claude.ai
- Fixed the /mcp "Connect on claude.ai" check saying "not connected" when claude.ai has a connector at the server's URL without its query
- Fixed `/install-github-app` and `/design-login` showing a generic failure for an account on hold instead of the on-hold notice and appeal link
- Fixed a running MCP task being reported as stopped when you move a session to the background; the background session can now follow the task, but not if its server uses stdio or sets headers
- Fixed self-hosted runners ignoring a session until they exited, after its failure report was lost or the session was given back to the same runner
- Fixed self-hosted sessions losing the prompt cache and earlier thinking when the list of repositories a restart couldn't prepare changed
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed tool calls behind a permission prompt vanishing with no result when a new runner took over the prompt, in sessions with telemetry off
- Fixed resumed self-hosted runner sessions starting without their pushed work in large repositories when `--push-outcome-on-release` is set
- Fixed self-hosted runner sessions being shown as working when Claude Code hangs at every start and `--startup-timeout-min` is from 2 to about 6
- Fixed `pkill -f` in self-hosted runner sessions on Linux ending its own shell with exit code 144, or the runner (needs a `pkill` with `--ignore-ancestors`)
- Fixed scheduled tasks on self-hosted runners having no tool to notify their owner when telemetry is off or a third-party provider is used
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed one slow `spawn-runner` hook keeping the orchestrator from claiming sessions for its free slots; it now polls every 4 to 6 seconds while a slot is free
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed a 403, such as an IP allowlist's, logged as a bad secret or token: most such lines now lead with the server's reason, so update log alerts that match the old words
- Fixed self-hosted runners' warn mode for repository settings stopping at the first finding of most kinds: it now goes on, up to 50 for a session, and says if it stops early
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed runners that start on a full disk taking sessions and failing them; they now wait for room and exit 1 after a minute with no session, unless started from a work order
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed a failed start suggesting a retry when the runner's machine had no git credentials; the error now says whom to ask and what to do if the repository is wrong
- Fixed the self-hosted runner's `last_poll_age_seconds` reading 0 while the runner had never polled successfully
- Fixed the notice about a skipped scheduled task that names no organization: it now says to start Claude Code with `--resume`, because `/resume` inside a running session doesn't run the task
- Fixed `claude plugin validate` wrongly warning that a mod's `AbovePrompt` or `AbovePromptList` hook never runs in VS Code
- Fixed `/design-sync` deleting a file it had just uploaded when Claude Design stored that file under a changed name
- Reverted 2.1.329's removal of the automatic retry when `max_tokens` exceeds a model's or gateway's limit
- Improved the claude.ai sign-in link shown by /login, `claude auth login` and `claude setup-token`: it is now much shorter
- Windows: Improved Grep and Glob speed by no longer starting a console host for each built-in ripgrep search on a local path
- Improved the speed of file diffs
- Improved `/config` search: most settings whose name starts with what you type come first, "effort" finds Model, and "dark" or "light" finds Theme
- Improved `/resume`: sessions where you only opened a screen such as `/model` and left are no longer listed
- Improved Reconnect in `/mcp` and `/plugin`: a server's page now stays open, with the cause in view, when the server still fails or needs sign-in
- Improved the error on macOS when sandbox deny lists are too long: it now names the long lists and how to shorten them
- Improved `/plugin` in fullscreen mode: the page of a plugin with errors now starts with those errors
- Improved `/ultrareview`'s cost confirmation on Team and Enterprise plans: it now says how much of your monthly spend limit is left when that is less than a review usually costs
- Improved self-hosted runner sessions on Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud's Agent Platform to say so when they start on another default model because your account refused the first
- Windows: Improved the error when a session's folder is on a drive Claude Code can't verify: it says why, and whether retrying can help
- Improved Code Mode: Claude is now told how to look at images and PDFs
- Improved Code Mode: after Esc, "Interrupted" now shows under the stopped command in place of a red error
- Improved Code Mode: the terminal freezes for far less time after a subagent's script makes thousands of tool calls
- Changed recurring scheduled tasks and `/loop` to run up to 30 days instead of 7 while their session keeps running, and say when they end; tasks made before this release still end at 7 days
- Changed more `rm` commands aimed at the root, home, a top-level folder or the working folder to ask for approval; where nobody can answer, they're refused
- Changed `deniedMcpServers` name entries to hide only the named claude.ai connector, not others at its URL; to block them all, deny its exact URL
- Changed `claude --teleport` in some setups to print the git commands for switching branch instead of running them; with `-p` it exits 1 until you switch
- Changed unrecognized model names containing "sonnet" or "haiku" to use the shorter system prompt, like other unrecognized names; `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT=0` gives every model the full one
- Changed skills that Claude runs with a `model` setting, other than `context: fork` skills, to leave subagents, forks, compaction and `/recap` on the session's model
- Changed a subagent's model fallback to carry over: agents with no model and forks it then starts run on the fallback, and the agents they start use its Bedrock region
- Self-hosted runner: Changed `spawn-runner` hooks to start while earlier ones still run, up to `--hook-concurrency` per orchestrator (4 by default); set it to 1 if yours can't run beside another
- Self-hosted runner: Changed Bash commands to skip the file diff when nothing needs it, so transcripts can lack it; set `bashEditDiffEnabled` to true in managed settings to get every diff
- Changed self-hosted runners to stop a session's start at once, without trying other runners, when a checkout hook exits with status 108
- Changed prompt hooks to accept model aliases such as `haiku` or `sonnet` in their `model` field
- Changed `/design-sync`'s fallback build of the reference Storybook to use only a Storybook installed in the project
- Changed subagent progress summaries in terminal sessions signed in to a Claude apps gateway to be written from short notes instead of the whole conversation, using far fewer tokens
- [VSCode] Added `/fork` to fork a conversation after its last reply (anthropics/claude-code#69272)
- [VSCode] Added `/workflows`, which opens the agent map with running workflows
- [VSCode] Added the `claudeCode.escapeStopsClaude` setting; turn it off so Escape does not stop Claude (anthropics/claude-code#91536)
- [VSCode] Added the `claudeCode.pinPrompt` setting to let your message scroll away instead of staying pinned
- [VSCode] Added the `claudeCode.contextUsageThreshold` setting for when the context indicator shows (anthropics/claude-code#93036)
- [VSCode] Added a `prompt` argument to the "Open in Side Bar" command for keybindings and extensions
- [VSCode] Added Move up and Move down to a session group's menu (anthropics/claude-code#98654)
- [VSCode] Fixed VS Code opening and focusing its terminal on every prompt of a connected terminal session
- [VSCode] Fixed copying a code block adding a trailing newline that ran the command on paste (anthropics/claude-code#96976)
- [VSCode] Fixed holding Enter on `/rewind` restoring files, and a double click on Remove or Delete removing a memory, MCP server or plugin marketplace, without confirmation
- [VSCode] Fixed Enter on a question card sending your earlier answer instead of picking the focused one, and arrow keys not working after an "Other" answer; answered questions reopen on your pick
- [VSCode] Fixed a held-down Enter key sending a half-written message or running a typed slash command
- [VSCode] Fixed Cmd+A, C, V, X and Z not working in the rename box and dialogs on macOS
- [VSCode] Fixed Ctrl+F and Ctrl+P not moving the caret in the message box on macOS
- [VSCode] Fixed the Accept and Reject buttons doing nothing on a proposed diff moved to a new window
- [VSCode] Fixed Accept and Reject Proposed Changes showing over the chat, the terminal tab and other files; they now show only on the proposed diff
- [VSCode] Fixed a slow-starting Claude tab taking the keyboard away from the file you had gone on typing in
- [VSCode] Fixed unsaved changes and new problems being missed on macOS and Linux for files whose path contains `#`, `?` or `%20`, such as a `C#` folder
- [VSCode] Fixed whole-line selections counting one line too many in the selection chip, in @-mentions and in what Claude is told, and file links leaving out the last line of a range
- [VSCode] Fixed a conversation forked in the panel re-running an old, unanswered prompt by itself after a window reload
- [VSCode] Fixed a forked conversation running the original conversation's `/loop` schedules a second time

- [VSCode] Fixed the plan preview's Add Comment button vanishing after a fast double click on a word
- [VSCode] Fixed long lines cut off in the Edit Notebook Cell row, permission rules squeezed in a narrow panel, hard-to-see question card marks, and menus moving the chat after a declined trust prompt

#### 2.1.329

- Added a trust dialog warning that says where a folder's hooks are declared
- Added a warning in the conversation, in Claude Desktop and other non-interactive hosts, when hooks in managed settings fail to load
- Added this session's scheduled tasks, `/loop` wakeups, the goal and this conversation's forks to `/tasks`; x stops one after asking
- Added a "Server message" row to a server's page in `/mcp` that shows the JSON-RPC error message of a remote HTTP MCP server that refuses the connection
- Added a "Marketplace auto-update" row to `/status` that names managed marketplaces that get no automatic updates, and why
- Added support for turning on Code Mode while OpenTelemetry events and metrics are enabled; each tool call the code makes sends its events; tracing still keeps it off
- Fixed `~/.claude.json` sometimes being reset to defaults when a network stall or file lock made it unreadable and cleared during a save

- Fixed `/terminal-setup` corrupting VS Code settings or keybindings files around block comments, and reporting success while losing the Shift+Enter binding where keybindings.json has an unclosed string
- Fixed files accepted through the IDE diff being saved without their last newline, and losing their byte order mark (BOM) when an edit was accepted by saving the diff in VS Code
- Fixed picking a cloud session in `/teleport` replacing your open conversation: the pick now starts a new session, as `/clear` does, and `/resume` brings the old one back
- Fixed `/usage-credits` asking Pro and Max users to log in again after opening the browser, and the link disappearing after 8 seconds if the browser doesn't open and a task stops for usage credits
- Fixed `/usage` saying usage credits are off when they had run out or reached the monthly limit, and `/model` not telling Pro and Max users when that limit blocks a model that runs on usage credits
- Fixed the spend limit menu showing your spend as your monthly limit and wrapping its rows under the pointer in narrow windows
- Fixed a status line script that prints without end freezing the prompt and using gigabytes of memory
- Fixed an empty, frozen screen after approving managed settings while the --resume picker, the trust dialog or another set-up screen was waiting
- Fixed choosing Default in `/model` replacing your saved model with your organization's default when the Default row already showed your saved model
- Fixed an MCP server being signed in again after you cleared its authentication while a token refresh was running
- Fixed background MCP tasks that stalled after a slow reconnect: Claude Code now reconnects most HTTP MCP servers by itself when one is left on an older protocol version
- Fixed PDFs, images and `.docx`, `.xlsx` or `.pptx` files that MCP servers or websites send as `application/octet-stream` being saved as .bin, which kept Claude from reading the PDFs and images

- Fixed `/code-review` stopping at a permission prompt, on most models, to look for a `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` that doesn't exist
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed `--push-outcome-on-release` sometimes deleting a session's branch on the git host
- Fixed Code Mode hiding a script's finished edits and the stopped command after Esc, and losing them on exit
- Fixed a runaway loop in Code Mode filling the machine's memory; it is now stopped at a limit
- Fixed a background agent running on when it was stopped while it was being resumed
- Fixed background shell commands using memory for the earlier conversation until they exit
- Fixed Remote Control using memory for the earlier conversation after a compaction or `/clear` in sessions run by Claude Desktop, IDEs or the SDK
- Fixed Stop not ending a request in Claude Desktop sessions on Bedrock while it waits on a hung AWS credential_process or sign-in call
- Fixed Claude sometimes failing to send you a file on its first try on Opus 4.8 and Opus 5
- Fixed Claude not being told that a connected MCP server's tools could not be loaded, and taking it for a server with no tools, in sessions with tool search

- Fixed auto mode asking for manual approval to `rm` a symlink that points outside the working directory or at itself
- Fixed `/sandbox` on Linux listing `allowUnixSockets` entries as allowed: they don't open those sockets there, and `/sandbox` now says so

- Fixed a removed plugin's MCP server staying connected in headless sessions after `reload_plugins` or when the account's plugin list drops it
- Fixed the Claude Docs connector's tools going missing when a plugin or MCP server at the same address failed to connect, and its error wrongly suggesting `/login`
- Fixed a new skills, commands or agents folder being missed when `--add-dir` names the working directory or Claude Code starts in the home folder
- Fixed sessions started from a pre-warmed process ignoring the `autoCompactWindow` setting in the project's `.claude/settings.json`
- Fixed `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` staying in effect in a running session after it is removed from settings.json

- Fixed a false "Couldn't save this change" warning after adding a permission rule or directory in a subfolder or worktree whose own `.claude/settings.local.json` is unreadable or malformed
- Fixed cloud sessions telling Claude to run a network proxy check after a failed request, which auto mode then blocked
- Fixed headless rewind and fork going ahead while a message sent right after a model change still waited on it
- Fixed Claude not being told when a background task was stopped while a cloud session was restarting
- Fixed `/team-onboarding` reporting a guide as shared on Team and Enterprise plans when the server refused the upload
- Fixed panels and questions being cut off at the prompt in fullscreen, `/help`, history search and the background tasks list losing rows or titles in short windows, and tables wrapping in dialogs
- Fixed resumed sessions showing "Rejected" or "Declined" for edits, questions and plans that were cut off when the session ended
- Fixed `/passes` showing the wrong number of passes after a server error, and offering usage credits for sharing when no guest passes are left

- Fixed `/terminal-setup` turning on "Use Option as Meta key" in Terminal.app on macOS 27, and tips there suggesting Option+Enter instead of Shift+Enter
